title: Cylindrical object
spec: Start by creating a new coordinate system with the Euler angles set to zero degrees and the translation vector also set to zero. Next, draw a two-dimensional sketch on a new face. Within this face, create a single loop and draw a circle with its center at coordinates [0.0469, 0.0469] and a radius of 0.0469 units. After drawing the circle, apply a scaling factor of 0.0937 to the entire two-dimensional sketch. Ensure that the sketch plane remains aligned with the original coordinate system by rotating it using the Euler angles [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] and translating it using the vector [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]. To transform the two-dimensional sketch into a three-dimensional model, extrude the sketch along the normal direction by a depth of 0.75 units, ensuring that the extrusion does not occur in the opposite direction. This operation will result in a new solid body. The final dimensions of the cylindrical object are a length of 0.09375 units, a width of 0.09375 units, and a height of 0.75 units. The object has a flat top and bottom, a smooth surface, and a uniform diameter throughout.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Define the initial coordinate system
workplane = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create the sketch for the base of the cylinder
sketch = (
    workplane
    .center(0.0469, 0.0469)  # Move to the center of the circle
    .circle(0.0469)          # Draw the circle
)

# Extrude the sketch to create the cylinder
cylinder = (
    sketch
    .extrude(0.75)           # Extrude the circle to create the cylinder
)

# Assign the final model to 'r'
r = cylinder

# Display the final model
